name: GPU time per frame in the macOS benchmark

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

hypothesisMarkdown: The benchmark only measures CPU time, so a change that moves work to the GPU (tile composition, blur) looks free. Metal's GPUStartTime/GPUEndTime on each command buffer gives the GPU time per frame without changing rendering.
measurementPlanMarkdown: Record GPUEndTime-GPUStartTime in the Metal completed handler behind a runtime flag (off by default), have the benchmark enable it for the measured frames, and report gpu_ms in the result JSON and in the report tables. Confirm it is populated and plausible on three scenarios, fast mode off and on.
reportMarkdown: gpu_ms is populated (mean, p50, p95, p99, max) and consistent with the scenarios: effects-cards costs 5.4 ms of GPU per frame, text-typing 1.6 ms. Finding: scroll-div-cards with fast mode on spends 27% more GPU time than with it off (2.61 vs 2.06 ms, p95 3.29 vs 2.09) because it composites tile textures; its CPU saving is partly paid on the GPU, still well inside a 8.3 ms frame at 120 Hz. No renderer behaviour changed.
decisionMarkdown: Keep. The metric is opt-in at runtime and only the benchmark turns it on. Future GPU-side work (tile texture size, blend passes) can now be judged.
